| [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) | GCN | A two-layer network that multiplies node features by the renormalized adjacency beats the 2016 semi-supervised baselines on three citation graphs and NELL. Read in full, including both appendices. | Read |
| [NOTE-381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-381.md) | The bottleneck of GNNs | Over-squashing: exponentially many messages forced through fixed-size vectors. GNNs stop fitting a synthetic tree task at depth 4–5. A fully adjacent last layer cuts QM9 error 42% without retuning, where doubling width gives 5.5%. Main text and appendices B and E read, the rest skimmed. | Read |
| [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) | TransE | Relations as translations, h + r ≈ t, trained with a margin ranking loss against corrupted triples. Fewer parameters and better link prediction than the matrix-per-relation models of its time, and the source of FB15k and filtered ranking. Read in full. | Read |
| [NOTE-383](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-383.md) | One for All (OFA) | Text-embedded features and a prompt graph with class nodes let one GNN train on citation, knowledge-graph and molecule datasets together. It matches or beats per-dataset GNNs on most supervised tasks. Zero-shot transfer to unseen graphs is weak, and joint training hurts link tasks. Read in full, with the dataset-construction appendix skimmed. | Read |
| [NOTE-384](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-384.md) | MPNN | Eight earlier graph networks are one form: summed messages, a node update, an invariant readout. Searching that space on QM9 gives a model at chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 targets, relative to DFT labels and on one random split. Long-range mechanisms, a master node or set2set, help most when geometry is withheld. Main text read in full, supplement skimmed. | Read |
| [NOTE-385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-385.md) | GNNs exponentially lose expressive power | A ReLU GCN's features approach the component-and-degree subspace at rate (sλ)^l. | [NOTE-386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-386.md) | LSPE | Random-walk return probabilities make a strong positional encoding with no sign ambiguity, and most of the ZINC gain comes from putting them at the input. | [NOTE-387](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-387.md) | EGNN | Equivariance without spherical harmonics: messages see squared distances, coordinates move along relative position vectors. | [NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md) | NequIP | Tensor-valued equivariant features in a message-passing interatomic potential, with large accuracy gains over invariant models at 1,000 configurations and a learning curve that looks steeper. | [NOTE-391](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-391.md) | Over-squashing via curvature | Over-squashing measured as a Jacobian bounded by powers of the normalized adjacency. Small gains on node classification, largest on heterophilic graphs. Main text read, appendix definitions and experimental details skimmed. | Read |

| [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md) | Survey on oversmoothing | Over-smoothing defined as exponential decay of a node-similarity measure, with Dirichlet energy as the canonical one and Mean Average Distance ruled out. | [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md) | Deeper insights into GCNs | A GCN layer is symmetric Laplacian smoothing. Co- and self-training help GCNs at very low label rates. Read in full. | Read |
